newsitem.title: BELARUS: World Bank may renew Belarus credits soon.
newsitem.headline: World Bank may renew Belarus credits soon.

text.p: The World Bank expects to sign a memorandum with the Belarus government soon to renew credits to the former Soviet republic, bank representative Christopher Willoughby said on Tuesday.
The bank is prepared to issue credits of $100 million a year providing Belarus complies with conditions to liberalise its financial market and restructure the economy.
Willoughby said the bank was waiting for the government to take such steps, and said nothing had been accomplished to remove barriers to hard currency trading.
The memorandum would commit the Belarussian government to ensuring convertibility of the Belarussian rouble by mid-year.
Willoughby said the government feared both an inflation spike and speculative activity against the rouble's level, due to the bank's low reserves.
He added it was possible the memorandum would not be signed.
The bank has already issued Belarus $170 million in credits.

Belarus's central bank ordered all banks and businesses to sell to it 30 percent of their hard currency at least once a month, effective this week. Last week it limited sales of hard currency by Belarussians to $200 from $500.
